headline: South Asia: North Korea says test of intermediate-range strategic missile included use of AI
script:
Good afternoon. This is your global conflict briefing.

BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT:
- South Asia: North Korea says test of intermediate-range strategic missile included use of AI.
- Persian Gulf Region: Five killed as Kyiv and Moscow trade strikes, Russia hits second bridge.
- India: 'Attacked with hammer': RSS functionary Rameshwar Tiwari dies after assault in UP.

Full breakdown follows.

NORTH AMERICA
United States - bottom line: Naval Special Warfare Command failed to identify, treat TBI in service members: Watchdog.
- Military Times, 23 hours ago: Naval Special Warfare Command failed to identify, treat TBI in service members: Watchdog.
The DOD Inspector General found that Naval Special Warfare Command failed to identity and treat traumatic brain injuries in personnel.
The Caribbean - bottom line: UDC warns it cannot guarantee daily services at Little Dunn’s River.
- Jamaica Gleaner, 13 hours ago: UDC warns it cannot guarantee daily services at Little Dunn’s River.
The Urban Development Corporation (UDC) says the relevant team has been directed to take steps to facilitate public access to Little Dunn’s River Beach in Ocho Rios, St Ann, in compliance with a court order. However, the UDC indicated that it was not in a position at this time to provide “day-to-day management” of the popular recreational spot, including arrangements for security, lifeguard services, sanitation, maintenance or other amenities ordinarily required for such a facility. The UDC is the state entity that owns the facility.
- Jamaica Gleaner, 13 hours ago: Docs to decide on next steps in response to delayed IDT ruling.
More than 100 junior doctors at the Mandeville Regional Hospital in Manchester stayed off the job on Friday, joining hundreds of colleagues across the island. The junior doctors abstained from work in an effort to pressure the Industrial Disputes Tribunal (IDT) to give a ruling in its overtime and incentive dispute with the Government or outline a timeline for its award.

ASIA
South Asia - bottom line: North Korea says test of intermediate-range strategic missile included use of AI.
- Dawn (Pakistan), South China Morning Post - China, The Hindu - International, Yonhap News Agency, NK News, NDTV - Top Stories, Taipei Times, just now: North Korea says test of intermediate-range strategic missile included use of AI.
North Korea said it tested an intermediate-range strategic missile on Saturday that involved the use of AI, hours after Seoul said Pyongyang had launched a ballistic missile. The launch took place days after Seoul’s military demanded an apology from Pyongyang for a blast that wounded three South Korean soldiers in the Demilitarised Zone (DMZ) that it blamed on the North. Pyongyang has denied responsibility for last month’s explosion and called South Korea “despicable” on Friday, undercutting overtures by Seoul’s civilian leadership seeking a return to dialogue.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 8 hours ago: 11 terrorists killed during operations in KP, Balochistan: state media.
Security forces killed 11 terrorists during intelligence-based operations (IBOs) in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and Balochistan, state media reported on Saturday. State-run Radio Pakistan reported that five Fitna al-Khawarij terrorists had been killed during an IBO in KP’s South Waziristan district. Quoting security sources, the report said that security forces were continuing effective operations against Fitna al-Khawarij in KP under the Azm-i-Istehkam vision.

- Dawn (Pakistan), 16 hours ago: Govts should be allowed to complete their terms: CM Maryam.
LAHORE: Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz has said governments that perform well should be allowed to complete their five-year terms, arguing that the lack of policy continuity in Pakistan remains a major hurdle to development. She was addressing a delegation of the National Command Authority Senior Officers Leadership Course on Thursday, according to an official handout.
India - bottom line: 'Attacked with hammer': RSS functionary Rameshwar Tiwari dies after assault in UP.
- Times of India - Top Stories, 6 hours ago: 'Attacked with hammer': RSS functionary Rameshwar Tiwari dies after assault in UP.
Rameshwar Tiwari was killed following an assault during a clash in Bheekam Chhapra village. His wife, Amrita Devi, filed an FIR against several named and unnamed individuals involved in the incident. Four police personnel have been suspended due to negligence in handling the situation prior to the attack. The conflict reportedly stemmed from an old land property issue between families in the area.

- Times of India - Top Stories, one hour ago: Russia to take 70,000 Indian skilled workers this year, Jaishankar tells panel.
External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar briefed a parliamentary committee on India's engagement with Russia and Ukraine. He highlighted bilateral trade expansion and India's aim to send skilled workers. The minister discussed India's diplomatic efforts to facilitate dialogue for ending the Ukraine conflict. Additionally, he noted the government's initiatives to release Indian nationals in the Russian military. Jaishankar emphasized India's commitment to secure economic interests and safeguard Indian citizens abroad.
- Times of India - Top Stories, 5 hours ago: 'Parents oppose marriage': Andhra man kills 19-year-old girlfriend, jumps to death.
Mahalakshmi, a young woman of 19, lost her life after a brutal knife attack by her ex-boyfriend, Chinna Rao, aged 22. The assault occurred at her home, where Chinna's persistent harassment, stemming from family opposition, culminated in violence. Mahalakshmi suffered grave injuries and passed away after four hours in the hospital. In a heartbreaking conclusion, Chinna leaped from a building, ending his life shortly after the attack.

The circumstances remained unclear but in recent weeks Aramco, majority-owned by the Saudi state, has come under attack from the Houthi group targeting the kingdom as part of the war in Yemen where Riyadh is backing the internationally recognised government. The troops were among more than 47,000 military personnel involved in the Tsentr-2026 – or Centre-2026 – drills in the central western Chelyabinsk region from Monday until Saturday.
